To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dielectric constant of ceramic-polyethylene composites at microwave frequencies can be predicted by using the exponential mixing rules with filler particles of prolat spheroid and the order of 0.3 to 0.5.
the dielectric constants for ceramic composites with high dielectric constant fillers and polyethelene matrix are measured and analyzed by different mixing rules.
the microwave dielectric properties are studied in this work.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dielectric properties of ceramic-polyethylene composite at the microwave frequency.
the dielectric constant measurement and the dielectric constant mixture rule for ceramic/polyethylene binary composites.
the dielectric constants for ceramic composites with high dielectric constant fillers and low dielectric constant matrix.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rule derived from prolate spheroids with low filler concentration has the best accuracy in estimation.

the rule derived from the filler particle of prolate sphaeroid is better for the estimation of dielectric constant of composites with filler concentration lower than 0.5 and the rule of exponential with order of 1.3 to 1.5 is suitable for higher filler concentration.

the rule derived from the filler particles of prolat spheroid with the order of filler concentration of 1/5 and exponential rules with order of 1 to 1/3 have the best accuracy for the estimation of dielectric constant for ceramic composites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dielectric constant of ceramic dispersions is a complex function of the dielectric constant and the concentration of filler particles.

the mixture rules derived from filler particles with prolate spheroidal shape and exponential rules with order of 1/n, n = 1/3, 1/4, and 1/5 can be used to estimate the dielectrics constants of high dielectric constant ceramics.
the dielectric constants for composites with low filler concentration are more sensitive to the mixing rules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dielectric properties of composites with high dielectric ceramic fillers and polymer matrix can be estimated with reasonable accuracy by using mixture laws.
a simple exponential mixing law with the order of filler concentration of 1/5 can be used to predict the microwave dielectric properties for ceramic-polymer composites.
it is possible to use microwave measurements to estimate the dielectrics of pure materials.
